findings.F1: The tested slope runs against the idea: on the 406 pooled 7-day grid cases with forecast < 0 (BTC and ETH only, since BNB did not run), the excess 7-day return rises with the length of the below-50 run (slope +0.00042 per day, t +1.15), and it also rises on log length (t +0.68), so the result is not a "right side but too small" one.
findings.F2: The below-50 state as a whole is followed by lower returns: mean excess 7-day return is -0.0101 (t -1.90, n 406), and the below-minus-above difference is -0.0133 at 7 days (Welch t -1.69, 330 vs 389 cases) and -0.0024 at 1 day (t -2.16, 2334 vs 2788 cases).
findings.F3: That weakness sits in fresh stretches and fades or reverses in old ones: excess 7-day return is -0.0223 for runs of 1–3 days (t -2.48, n 92), -0.0143 for 4–7 days (n 52), +0.0007 for 8–14 days (n 72), -0.0204 for 15–28 days (n 71) and +0.0214 for runs over 28 days (t +1.19, n 43); this ending reversal is what turns the tested slope positive.
findings.F4: The fresh-versus-old gap holds in both coins and both halves of the windows: runs of 7 days or less against longer runs give -0.0150 vs -0.0031 in BTC (83 and 114 cases), -0.0161 vs -0.0096 in ETH (76 and 133 cases), -0.0124 vs -0.0068 in w1–12, and -0.0185 vs -0.0064 in w13–24.
findings.F5: The effect is drowned by the market's own years: fresh-run excess returns are strongly negative in 2018 (-0.050), 2019 (-0.022) and 2022 (-0.061) but positive in 2020 (+0.018), 2023 (+0.005) and 2024 (+0.006), and the per-year slope t ranges from -0.77 to +2.25.
findings.F6: The depth of RSI below 50 does not grade the move: mean excess 7-day return is -0.007 at RSI 0–30, -0.006 at 30–40, -0.017 at 40–45 and -0.008 at 45–50, and RSI's 7-day change has no slope among below-50 bars (t -0.07, n 319).

ideas.idea: The fewer days a coin's 14-day RSI has stayed below 50 without a break, counted in days up to the close, the lower its return over the next 7 days.
ideas.consequence: A fresh drop of RSI below its midpoint is a reason to stay out of or short the coin for the following week, while a long-standing stretch below 50 is not.
ideas.name: fresh RSI break continues down

ideas.idea: The more days a coin's 14-day RSI has stayed below 50 without a break, counted in days up to the close, the higher its return over the next 7 days, only once the stretch has lasted longer than about four weeks.
ideas.consequence: A very long, unbroken stretch of seller control is a reason to cover shorts rather than add to them for the following week.
ideas.name: exhausted RSI downtrend rebounds
